wintercity_e15_entry.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_entry.text: On Day 913, Yue collected eighteen copper for the second completed seasonal week, the nine hours on Days 907, 909, and 911. The public keeper checked the record and paid the actual sum. Yue paid eight for the inn week through Day 919 under the continuing notice terms, with food separate. The next public sessions would be Days 914, 916, and 918. Their future eighteen would be due only after completion, at the Day 920 settlement.

wintercity_e15_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_001.text: The Day 926 clinic fee stayed reserved from owned money. Her current reduced comparator permission did not cover a coupled task, prolonged holding, or heavy lifting. Yue took a light morning walk and returned before the ordinary posture tired. The optional factory afternoons on Days 921 through 923 still stood in the accepted roster, with a possible twelve copper for six completed hours. They had not yet been worked or paid, and no private bench authority accompanied them.

wintercity_e15_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_002.text: Du Ling arrived at the proper public request desk with three current city account holders. Their sources concerned the waiting corner's actual closure and the gap before the public room opened, not mine interviews or private apparatus methods. Each person had brought a separate statement and a proposed use permission. Ling asked Yue whether she would consider carrying or reading the agreed material. The request did not make Yue a delegate until a particular scope was actually accepted.

wintercity_e15_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_003.text: The first account holder, an early-shift packer named Lan He, described waiting outside between the private corner's closing date and the later public opening. His dated ordinary journey record supported the times. He would allow a redacted public account and wanted his employer and address removed. He retained the original. Yue could not copy those identifiers into a supposedly anonymous appendix or borrow his work credential to enter a private room. His permission was useful precisely because its actual limits were clear.

wintercity_e15_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_004.text: The second holder, a washhouse customer named Su Mei, wanted a later interval suited to her own travel. She had a dated public passage slip and notes made that morning. She would authorize a sealed factual submission to the hearing clerk, but not public narration under her name or voice. A public summary could say that another consented request concerned a later interval only if she checked and approved its exact redacted words. Yue asked her to do that herself.

wintercity_e15_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_005.text: The third holder, an ordinary room keeper named Fan Zhi, had a consented redacted staffing total for the expired corner. The account showed the number of paid keeper hours and actual source allowance, with personal wages and client identities removed. He was authorized by the record owner to send that redacted total to the hearing and public proposal file. He could not hand Yue the original private payroll or every room key. The total would support a cost comparison without pretending that source fuel was the only expense.

wintercity_e15_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_006.text: Each person could choose not to work through Yue. The formal desk could receive authorized statements directly, and public waiting access did not depend on joining her position. Yue said that before asking about any role. Lan He still wanted a public reading; Su Mei still preferred a sealed account; Fan Zhi wanted the cost boundary accurately described. Their different choices would not be flattened into a single chorus just because one person might speak at the hearing.

wintercity_e15_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_007.text: Ning explained the hearing's source rules. Public narration could use only the exact public-authorized redactions. A sealed account would stay within the clerk's authorized custody and stated use. The record holder could withdraw an unsubmitted copy before its accepted deadline, but a properly submitted record would then follow the hearing's declared correction and custody procedure. A document's presence on Yue's table did not make it hers to publish, keep indefinitely, or use for a second unrelated dispute.

wintercity_e15_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_008.text: The hearing was scheduled during the later cold-term review, Days 948 through 954. A proposal needed real funding, an eligible room, qualified staffing, and accepted dates, not merely a persuasive statement about hardship. The present source collection could prepare a limited request for exit notice and service comparisons. No one promised that the owner would lose physically or be obliged to support a new universal room. The physical contest's valid result remained unchanged.

wintercity_e15_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_009.text: Yue asked which possible roles the holders actually wanted her to take. Lan He would permit her to become the public spokesperson for the limited redacted gap proposal. Su Mei would authorize delivery of the sealed statement, with the approved narrow public summary separately controlled. Fan Zhi would authorize use of the redacted staffing total in either an open proposal or sealed factual comparison. None granted a mandate over their wages, votes, future testimony, or private employment decisions.

wintercity_e15_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_010.text: Ling said the cooperative would vote on its priced calendar alternatives on Day 920. Yue could read the sources before that choice without promising how the members would vote. The group needed a credible cost comparison more than a heroic label. A public spokesperson would take a visible position and answer challenges at the hearing. A sealed carrier could deliver facts without that same public advocacy role. Yue could also decline both, returning the borrowed copies and keeping only her own observations.

wintercity_e15_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_011.text: She put the proposed source permissions beside the optional factory offer. Its accepted clause allowed authorized public safety reporting and preserved all earned wages. It also let the factory withdraw this future discretionary job and client meeting invitation if she chose the public spokesperson role in this particular dispute. No future twelve had been earned. Selecting that visible role would therefore cost an actual six-hour opportunity and invitation, rather than subtracting an abstract reputation number while every door stayed open.

wintercity_e15_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_012.text: A sealed factual submission under the current permitted scope did not itself make her the public spokesperson. The factory keeper had confirmed that distinction in writing, without granting private source access to the hearing. If Yue chose that role and completed the later six hours safely, she could earn twelve and retain the bounded client invitation. She would lose the public speaking mandate Lan He had offered and would have to leave public advocacy to another consenting person.

wintercity_e15_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_013.text: Declining copied evidence would return the three loaned working copies by the actual deadline. Yue could still speak about her own public observation, with no authority to quote the holders' records or call herself their representative. The future factory job and invitation would remain under their original terms. The holders could submit directly or choose another carrier. No one would lose public service because Yue declined a role, and she would not get a cooperative endorsement for work she had not accepted.

wintercity_e15_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_014.text: On Day 914, she completed the week's first three-hour public reading session with its agreed pauses. The source question stayed outside the paid role; callers received the current notices regardless of their view of the hearing. She kept the statement copies sealed in the proper light cover rather than leave them beside public sheets. The keeper handled the registers and ordinary carrying. A private permission decision did not expand the job's access or remove the arm's present restriction.

wintercity_e15_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_015.text: Afterward, she met Lan He at the public request room to check the redaction. One sentence said every worker had needed the early corner. He agreed that his own account could not support that broad claim. They changed it to his actual experience and the particular gap he wanted considered. Yue did not call the correction disloyalty. A limited accurate statement could survive scrutiny better than a sweeping one that made other workers' choices disappear.

wintercity_e15_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_016.text: Su Mei checked the proposed public summary herself. She approved one sentence saying a separate consented application sought later access, with no identifying details. She declined a longer phrase that implied she backed the early workers' full calendar. Yue removed it. The sealed account retained its own real dates and preferred interval. Two needs could enter one hearing without being represented as the same wish or treated as evidence that the speaker must receive complete control over both.

wintercity_e15_017.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_017.text: Fan Zhi compared the redacted cost sheet against his authorized copy. A quoted total had left out the cleanup hour. They corrected it before any submission. Yue did not add a new unpaid helper to make the proposal cheaper after discovering the actual staffing cost. The future room alternatives would need to fund their chosen keeper schedule, including accepted cleanup. The correction changed a practical budget that members would actually have to vote on, with no spiritual technique able to hide the missing wage.

wintercity_e15_018.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_018.text: On Day 915, Yue paid the public copy desk for a single one-copper working comparison she needed to read the current redactions. It belonged to the authorized preparatory scope and would be returned or submitted under the selected role. No private original was purchased. She kept that actual spent copper out of the future factory twelve and did not call it an investment guaranteed to return. A hearing might refuse the final proposal even after its sources were carefully prepared.

wintercity_e15_019.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_019.text: Qin Lu offered a listed half-hour scope reading for one copper. Yue accepted and asked her to compare the public spokesperson, sealed carrier, and source-return roles against the three actual permissions. She would read only those consented redactions, not obtain private payroll through a familiar advocate's name. The half-hour identified the same finite alternatives Ning had described. Lu could advise on the written boundaries, but the holders and Yue would still choose their own accepted actions.

wintercity_e15_020.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_020.text: The reading ended with a practical question: what would Yue say if the hearing rejected her preferred calendar? She said she would preserve the recorded reasons and current lawful services, not announce an unapproved room as if public emotion had opened it. Lu nodded and put the actual deadline beside the source list. An earned institutional change would need accepted terms after the discussion. Its possibility did not guarantee success or make her physical defeat a temporary illusion waiting to be reclassified.

wintercity_e15_021.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_021.text: On Day 916, the second three-hour public session completed another six-hour subtotal for the week. Yue read the current route notices, took the proper breaks, and sent a private billing question to the dispute clerk. Nobody in the queue was asked to support her possible hearing role in return. At home, she stopped a permitted reduced unloaded practice before starting it, because the longer posture had already made the forearm tired. Permission described a safe condition; it did not command use on every day.

wintercity_e15_022.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_022.text: That evening, she told Wen what the three roles would practically change, without revealing the sealed account's private details. She asked whether she would resent the lost twelve if she spoke publicly. Yue said she probably would, because money and access had actual value. Wanting the visible role did not make its cost imaginary. Wen did not tell her that courage would guarantee a better employer. She could choose with the real loss still included, rather than wait for a comforting promise nobody could substantiate.

wintercity_testimony_choice.speaker: narrator
wintercity_testimony_choice.text: By Day 917, the record holders had confirmed the final offered scopes and the proper submission deadline. Yue had the public redactions, approved narrow summary, sealed copy, and redacted cost total under their separate permissions. She would select one role before the desk closed that evening. The unselected roles remained available to other consenting people through the institution's actual procedure. She could carry a real mandate, a bounded sealed packet, or her own observations only. Each choice would alter future work and usable sources.

choices.text: Accept the public redacted spokesperson mandate; spend five and cancel the twelve-copper future factory job and client invitation.
Deliver only the consented sealed factual submission; spend three, keep the future job, and leave the public mandate to another speaker.
Return the borrowed sources for one copper; retain the future job and use only your own observations without an endorsement.

wintercity_testimony_public.speaker: narrator
wintercity_testimony_public.text: Yue accepted the limited public spokesperson mandate on Day 917. Lan He signed the exact authorized redaction, Su Mei confirmed the single narrow public summary and sealed-use permission, and Fan Zhi confirmed the redacted staffing total. Yue signed for those particular uses, not for the holders' future votes or private sources. She paid four copper for the approved public copies and one for their proper dispatch. The public position now had real prepared evidence and five spent copper.

wintercity_e15_public_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_public_001.text: She sent the optional factory desk her actual notice under the accepted clause. The keeper cancelled the six unperformed hours on Days 921 through 923 and removed the discretionary client meeting invitation. No twelve-copper wage was earned or owed. Her earlier completed factory wages, if any, remained paid, and the independent public reading appointment stayed intact. The lawful public safety reporting boundary also remained. A visible service stance had cost a real future job and access, without rewriting unrelated accounts.

wintercity_e15_public_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_public_002.text: The keeper returned the cancelled roster copy rather than leave Yue expecting a place next week. She checked that no borrowed client papers remained under this future role, because no such loan had begun. There was no private bench authority to lose or secretly keep. The ordinary public-stock work would go to another eligible speaker if the factory filled it. Yue did not announce that the other person had betrayed the workers merely by taking a different permissible role.

wintercity_e15_public_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_public_003.text: At the hearing desk, Ning registered the public redacted submission and sealed packet under their separate custody rules. Yue retained only her authorized public working copies and own observations, with the private sealed source in the proper institutional custody. The clerk stamped actual receipt. Submission was complete; approval of the room proposal was not. Yue could now prepare the public comparison within its mandate and answer questions about the cost total without inventing a broader confidential record.

wintercity_e15_public_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_public_004.text: Lan He thanked her for taking the visible role, then said he would still make his own work and cooperative choices. Su Mei wanted the later interval considered and had not become a supporter of every early-shift proposal. Fan Zhi asked her to keep the cleanup hour in the price. Yue agreed to those actual boundaries. Being chosen to speak did not make the sources flatter or give her authority to reward agreement with service access.

wintercity_e15_public_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_public_005.text: That evening, she put the lost six-hour factory opportunity in her ordinary account as twelve copper unearned, not twelve paid and later confiscated. The six cancelled hours would be free time unless another finite role was actually offered. Her five publication and dispatch copper were spent. The public mandate would carry through the prepared hearing, then need a defined closure. Yue could feel the cost and still choose it, with no guaranteed later stipend promised to make the tradeoff vanish.

wintercity_testimony_sealed.speaker: narrator
wintercity_testimony_sealed.text: Yue accepted the bounded sealed carrier role on Day 917 and declined the public spokesperson mandate. The three holders confirmed the uses their actual permissions allowed. The public-authorized redactions could accompany the factual comparison, while Su Mei's detailed account would stay sealed in the hearing clerk's declared custody. Yue paid two copper for the accepted custody preparation and one for proper dispatch. The three spent copper funded that actual submission, not a public coalition title.

wintercity_e15_sealed_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_sealed_001.text: She gave the optional factory keeper the role's exact written scope. Under the already confirmed distinction, the six two-hour afternoons on Days 921 through 923 remained booked, with twelve copper possible only after actual completion. The discretionary client meeting invitation also remained bounded under its original condition. No private bench or method right was added. Yue kept the independent public reading role separate and did not use her future factory seat to enter a hearing source room she had never been authorized to inspect.

wintercity_e15_sealed_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_sealed_002.text: At the formal desk, Ning registered the factual packet and gave Yue a receipt under its sealed-use rules. The borrowed sealed working copy went into authorized custody, and Yue retained only the redactions she could properly use and her own observations. She could later confirm delivery and answer within that factual carrier scope. She could not stand up at the hearing and claim the public spokesperson mandate she had declined, or quote Su Mei's private account to create an audience.

wintercity_e15_sealed_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_sealed_003.text: Lan He chose to look for another willing public speaker rather than make Yue's narrower role a betrayal. He retained control of his redacted statement and could authorize that separate use himself. Su Mei thanked Yue for preserving the sealed boundary. Fan Zhi pointed again to the cleanup hour in the redacted cost total. Their distinct responses remained real. A source carrier could do useful work without receiving every witness's loyalty or eliminating their need to make further choices.

wintercity_e15_sealed_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_sealed_004.text: Yue returned the unused public programme drafts and kept no unapproved version in her own file. The factory keeper would not receive the sealed account or private hearing papers simply because the paid afternoons remained scheduled. The client invitation had its own scope, and its source holders would have to authorize any later disclosure. Maintaining one paid opportunity required no leak between the records. Yue checked that boundary before putting the future work calendar beside the public roster.

wintercity_e15_sealed_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_sealed_005.text: Her ordinary account showed three copper spent on the selected packet and no twelve received yet. The public advocacy mandate was absent; another person could take it through actual consent. She would complete the future factory hours safely or give proper notice if the arm failed their ordinary limits. The narrower hearing role had preserved real employment and access while reducing what she could claim publicly. Neither outcome altered the owner's direct physical win or today's stage-seven condition.

wintercity_testimony_return.speaker: narrator
wintercity_testimony_return.text: Yue declined both copied-source roles on Day 917. She paid one copper to return the three holders' loaned working packets through the proper desk before the agreed deadline. The public comparison she had already bought for preparation was returned within that custody, not kept as an unauthorized private archive. Lan He retained his original and could choose another speaker. Su Mei kept her sealed-use decision, and Fan Zhi retained authority over the cost copy.

wintercity_e15_return_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_return_001.text: Ning signed for the actual return and marked Yue outside both mandates. She could still submit her own public observations, including the time and weather she had personally recorded at the bench. Those observations did not contain the holders' journey records, sealed account, or verified staffing total. She could not quote borrowed facts from memory after returning the papers and pretend their permissions still applied. The sources had owners and actual chosen uses beyond her preferred account of the dispute.

wintercity_e15_return_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_return_002.text: The optional factory desk kept the six two-hour afternoons on Days 921 through 923 under their existing terms. Twelve copper remained possible only after the six actual hours, with the clerk doing writing and carrying. The discretionary client invitation stayed available within its original scope. No private bench or permanent post appeared. Yue's independent public reading term remained separate. Keeping this opportunity did not give her a cooperative endorsement or secretly preserve the copied testimony she had declined.

wintercity_e15_return_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_return_003.text: Ling said the holders would decide their next formal route themselves. She did not withdraw washhouse information or turn the customers against Yue for refusing a mandate. Lan He was disappointed and asked another potential speaker. Su Mei preferred the returned sealed source to an unwilling carrier. Fan Zhi checked the copy list carefully and thanked her for a clean return. Yue heard those different answers without rewriting them into unanimous approval or punishment.

wintercity_e15_return_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_return_004.text: Yue prepared a short statement limited to her own observed uncovered interval. She did not add a verified staffing figure she no longer held or describe another person's needs as her public constituency. The hearing could consider that narrower observation under its own procedure. It might carry less weight than the consented source comparison. That reduced evidentiary strength was a real consequence of the choice, even while a future twelve-copper job and bounded client invitation remained available.

wintercity_e15_return_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_return_005.text: Her account showed one return-dispatch copper spent and no publication or custody fee bought on this path. She would not owe public advocacy work for a role never accepted. The future factory hours remained ordinary work to be completed under the arm's restrictions, not a reward for silence about public safety. Yue kept her own observations in a small cover and left the three returned sources out. The decision closed copied access without erasing the people who had chosen a different next step.

wintercity_testimony_after.speaker: narrator
wintercity_testimony_after.text: After the chosen source role was recorded, Yue put only the belongings she could actually retain into the light cover. Submitted sealed material stayed in authorized custody; returned working packets stayed with their holders. A missing acknowledgement would require a real check at the proper desk, not an assumption that she had every possible mandate. The independent public reader's roster remained the same. Her own clinic note and reduced comparator permission also remained current, with no powered task added to the source decision.

wintercity_e15_after_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_001.text: The next morning, Day 918, she completed the week's final three-hour public reading session. The keeper entered today's hours beside the two earlier mornings, making nine actually completed and eighteen payable on Day 920. Yue read the current public room hours without adding an unapproved cooperative alternative. Callers were not asked which hearing role she had selected before receiving the same information. The finite source choice could affect her future work without corrupting the present public service.

wintercity_e15_after_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_002.text: Ning handled a correction request from a caller who had put the wrong day on a formal application. The clerk explained the actual amendment procedure. Yue could read its public instructions, but would not alter the applicant's signed source herself or decide that the error proved the whole complaint false. The person corrected the date under the permitted process. An account could be improved by a supported change without pretending the original wrong entry had never existed.

wintercity_e15_after_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_003.text: During the break, a boy asked Yue if the hearing would make her stronger than Gao Shen. She said the direct comparison had already shown his greater qualified physical capacity. The hearing concerned specific terms and service proposals, not a cultivation contest. A changed exit notice could give people time to plan without supplying anyone new spiritual charge. The boy seemed disappointed, then asked whether the public bench would open earlier. Yue gave the actual current answer instead of a hopeful promise.

wintercity_e15_after_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_004.text: The keeper cleared a loose stack of replaced sheets from the public stand before closing. Yue returned her reader's copies and took only her own completed-hours receipt. The ordinary appointment did not authorize keeping the desk's master notices or callers' private papers. She walked to the inn by the light route and ate the listed simple meal. The arm had tolerated the day's seated work with breaks. She would not convert that comfort into an untested coupled source application.

wintercity_e15_after_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_005.text: Wen had an ordinary dispute with a supplier about six ribs ordered for umbrella repairs. Four matched the accepted measurement and two did not. The supplier offered to replace the two on the next actual delivery, returning the incorrect pieces now. Wen needed one repair sooner and chose to buy a separate suitable rib locally at its posted price. The choice cost real money and preserved the customer's booked interval. The supplier's future replacement would not make tonight's separate purchase unspent.

wintercity_e15_after_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_006.text: Yue listened in the common room while Wen counted the two returned pieces. She did not use qi to stretch the wrong ribs into a correct fit. Nor did she promise that the later delivery would arrive before its known route allowed. She had chosen an actual ordinary workaround and could decide whether to charge any extra under her customer agreement. The repair needed its own proper account, with no hearing role required to prove the value of a sound umbrella.

wintercity_e15_after_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_007.text: The customer accepted the finished repair after the agreed ordinary rain test. Wen received the original finite fee, taking the extra local rib cost from her own margin because she had promised that delivery interval. She did not blame Yue for the supplier or demand praise as compensation for doing what she had undertaken. She thought of Jia's forfeited deposit and found the conversation more useful than a speech about always trying one's best. Real work could include an acknowledged smaller profit.

wintercity_e15_after_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_008.text: On Day 919, Yue had no public reading session and used the morning for ordinary laundry within the current restrictions. The washhouse attendant carried the water and heavy wet cloth under the paid service. Yue sorted light dry pieces and did not pretend repeated wringing fit the reduced arm plan. The charge covered its actual listed work, not an unlimited private care arrangement. Ling greeted her without reopening the completed source decision as a condition of using the washhouse.

wintercity_e15_after_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_009.text: A customer wanted to know whether every person at the washhouse had signed a hearing statement. Ling said no. The service remained available under its ordinary terms, with testimony handled through separate voluntary permissions. Yue did not identify Su Mei or imply a private account had become public because customers asked. The boundary held in an ordinary queue where it mattered. People could wash, wait, disagree, and leave without being drafted into a coalition by proximity.

wintercity_e15_after_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_010.text: The paid attendant asked Yue which clean bundle was hers, using the ordinary receipt number. She answered, rather than describe everyone else's bundle from memory. A small mix-up could have taken someone else's clothing to the inn. The actual check prevented it. Yue carried only the light dry part allowed by her present note and used the paid return delivery for the heavier bundle. Its one-copper fee was a real current expense, not a free benefit of having once volunteered there.

wintercity_e15_after_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_011.text: At the courtyard, the puppet helper had a fever and cancelled the coming rehearsal interval before it began. Peng booked another competent paid helper already known to the committee rather than ask Yue to lift the frame. The replacement had his own fee and available hours. It meant a shorter rehearsal than Peng wanted. She accepted the actual limits instead of turning an injured visitor's desire to help into unsafe overhead work that a small circuit could not support.

wintercity_e15_after_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_012.text: Yue could read one brief narration line within her ordinary permitted posture, if Peng still wanted it. Peng thanked her and said today's rehearsal needed only the two operators and replacement frame helper. Yue accepted being unnecessary for that task. A capable planned team did not have to fail so her contribution could become indispensable. She watched from the public bench and let the paid people perform their own real work, with their chosen safe interval and equipment.

wintercity_e15_after_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_013.text: The younger operator had improved the missed cue since Day 903. The child author still wanted the final rhyme, and the shorter passage now reached it without rushing. Yue laughed at the stove's stubborn complaint again, noticing that the joke remained funny without a fresh lesson attached to it. Peng stopped at the paid room's actual closing time. The troupe's progress had come from rehearsed ordinary craft rather than waiting for a cultivator to grant confidence in one dramatic visit.

wintercity_e15_after_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_014.text: After the rehearsal, the musicians compared the available festival dance space with their planned tempo. Wet paving would reduce the usable area, so the committee kept the slower version it had tested earlier. A faster flourish would fit only if the weather and actual floor allowed it after inspection. Yue did not assure them the snow would disappear because the festival mattered. A good performance could use a smaller honest space rather than an imagined dry one.

wintercity_e15_after_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_015.text: A market stallholder asked whether the committee would pay for an extra lantern beside his private sign. The accepted programme funded the shared route lighting, not every individual stall decoration. He could buy his own inspected lamp or keep the current sign. The keeper explained the boundary and gave the public lighting plan. Yue could see the actual choices without treating his annoyance as a danger to be defeated. He chose to keep the sign and spend the money on stock.

wintercity_e15_after_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_016.text: At the inn, the younger singer practised in the earlier interval she had actually booked. Yue listened for a little while and then went upstairs, keeping her own rest. The singer's future audition had no promised result and would occur after the festival. Peng could introduce her to the proper application desk but had not granted a place on the programme. Yue enjoyed the sound without turning the applicant into an ally she must reward if a hearing went well.

wintercity_e15_after_017.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_017.text: Mrs Fen asked for residents' current plans before renewing the meal stock. Yue listed her public work mornings and ordinary days, with future optional work handled according to the selected source role's actual roster. She did not order food twice for mutually exclusive appointments. The innkeeper would buy from the stated current orders, not imagined wages. A missing confirmation required checking before a special meal was promised. The routine question made the decision's practical calendar visible.

wintercity_e15_after_018.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_018.text: Yue sorted the relevant source receipts and cancellation or continuation papers in separate covers. Her public reading term still ended on Day 962 unless properly changed through its own agreement. The prepared hearing had its declared later dates. The optional factory work, if retained, belonged to three finite afternoons and would need actual completion. She could not use one institution's stamp to extend another term. The physical loss and received care sat in their own light cover, without being erased by any new role.

wintercity_e15_after_019.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_019.text: She thought about the instinct to make every choice feel like the correct one after taking it. The actual source record would not oblige her to feel satisfied immediately. A public position might be worth its lost opportunity and still sting financially. A sealed role could be useful while leaving her outside a public mandate. Returning evidence could preserve work and reduce what she could substantiate. The different consequences were real; her feelings would have to live with the one she had chosen.

wintercity_e15_after_020.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_020.text: Lan He passed the inn door on his way home and asked only for the public vote time. Yue gave Day 920 at the listed committee room. He could attend if eligible under the cooperative's actual membership rule; she could not admit him by personal favour. His particular source permission remained what he had signed. The conversation did not reopen every earlier option or silently hand her an unchosen role. They parted with a useful date and their own next decisions.

wintercity_e15_after_021.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_021.text: Later, Su Mei sent a brief request through the proper desk asking that any public summary retain her approved wording. Ning confirmed that rule under the actual consent record. Yue did not need to know private delivery details to honour it. The holder's continuing agency was not an obstacle the protagonist had to overcome. It was part of why the source was usable at all. A careful hearing could accept a narrower account than an audience might have found most dramatic.

wintercity_e15_after_022.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_022.text: Fan Zhi's redacted cost total remained available only under the actual selected custody and mandate. The cleanup hour would not be omitted by a future priced proposal just to improve its apparent affordability. Yue reminded herself that no physical enthusiasm could pay an ordinary keeper for a shift not in the budget. The cooperative could fund its chosen interval, revise it, or decline. Its members would have to choose that actual use tomorrow, under a calendar they could honestly operate.

wintercity_e15_after_023.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_023.text: Before evening, a clerk returned a committee sheet whose title had called every waiting-space applicant a cooperative member. Several applicants were not members and had no vote over its fund. The keeper corrected the title to distinguish public requests from voting membership. Yue could still attend as an invited observer. She would not count her paid public reading hours as a purchased vote. A source account and a collective spending right needed their own actual bases.

wintercity_e15_after_024.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_024.text: The correction mattered to an older man who wanted the later interval but had never joined the cooperative. He could submit the public need and ask how membership worked; he could not spend the current members' reserve from outside their agreement. Ling offered the real application information and did not guarantee acceptance before tomorrow's vote. The man chose to keep his public request separate. His need could remain relevant even without a vote or a promise to join.

wintercity_e15_after_025.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_025.text: Yue heard a rumour that Gao Shen would pay for every room if he feared the public statement. She asked for its source before letting it enter her plans. Nobody had a signed offer or authorized budget. The rumour stayed out of the priced alternatives. An owner could be pressured to discuss a term and still decline to fund a broader service. Yue would not create an invisible future benefactor merely because it made the cooperative's present arithmetic more comfortable.

wintercity_e15_after_026.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_026.text: The members' prepared alternatives each listed the keeper's accepted wage, cleanup, eligible room, and compatible external source. One had an earlier two-hour interval; the other placed the same funded staffing later. They could also decline both and retain their reserve for another purpose. Yue read the public outline without implying which vote the hearing required. The room would open only under a final accepted plan, with members and paid staff able to refuse a duty not yet theirs.

wintercity_e15_after_027.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_027.text: At the window, she checked her mother's last received account rather than supply a fresh improvement from worry alone. The shoulder still needed shorter tasks and ordinary help. The finite support selected earlier had its actual record and expected report; it was not money available in Yue's own current purse. Baseline home assistance remained a separate chosen arrangement. No city hearing vote could guarantee that the next private letter would contain the news she most wanted.

wintercity_e15_after_028.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_028.text: She kept the promised correspondence date on her ordinary calendar. A one-copper dispatch bought a real carrier interval, not immediate knowledge at the far end. Her mother could answer in her own time and choose what private detail to share. Yue did not turn an anxious daughter's wish for certainty into authority over that reply. The future report would matter when it actually arrived. Tonight she could only preserve the known care commitments and her next sensible steps.

wintercity_e15_after_029.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_029.text: The singer downstairs finished at the booked hour, leaving the common room available for residents again. Bo showed the younger learner how to put the cold scrap away without leaving sharp pieces in the shared box. Yue watched from the chair and kept the injured arm light. Their ordinary competence made the room easier to share. No one needed to fail or become helpless to keep her at the centre of the evening.

wintercity_e15_after_030.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_030.text: When Fen checked the outer latch, Yue said goodnight and took the dry passage upstairs. The next day's independent wage would be received for work already done. The vote would belong to the eligible members, and the selected source role would keep its own real cost and permission boundaries.

wintercity_e15_after_031.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e15_after_031.text: Night brought colder air beneath the new curtain. The room's ordinary lamp had been filled from the inn's paid stock and stood clear of the paper decoration. Yue used its light to check the Day 920 pay desk hours, then put the completed-hours receipt away. Eighteen had been earned in the public week and remained to be physically received. The next morning would include that settlement and the members' own room vote, not an automatic victory promised by her source choice.
